prompt.adult: On the fourth day God set lights in the firmament. According to Genesis 1:14, what were they also to be for, along with days and years?
prompt.child: When God made the lights in the sky, they were for days and years. What else were they to be for?
prompt.teen: Genesis 1:14: “and let them be for” what, “and for days and years”?
prompt.older: According to Genesis 1:14, besides days and years, what were the lights to be for?

verses.text: Then God said, “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs and seasons, and for days and years;

explanation.child: Look right after “and let them be for” in verse 14.
explanation.teen: 1:14 names what the lights divide, then what they are for. Read the first pair.
explanation.older: It follows “and let them be for” in 1:14.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:15 says they were to give light on the earth. 1:17 says God set them in the firmament.
teaching.takeaway: God said the lights were to be for signs and seasons.

prompt.adult: Genesis 2:11 names the first river from Eden. In 2:20, after Adam named the cattle, the birds, and the beasts, what was not found for him?
prompt.child: Adam gave names to the animals. What does the verse say was still missing for him?
prompt.teen: Genesis 2:20: “But for Adam there was not found” what?
prompt.older: Read with 2:11, what does 2:20 say was not found for Adam?

choices.text: a garden east of the river
a rest from all his work

verses.text: The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one which skirts the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
So Adam gave names to all cattle, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper comparable to him.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 20.
explanation.teen: 2:11 names the first river; 2:20 ends with what was not found. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “there was not found” in 2:20.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:11 says the first river skirts the land of Havilah. 2:19 says God brought the beasts to Adam to see what he would call them.
teaching.takeaway: There was not found a helper comparable to him.

prompt.adult: Genesis 1:4 says God divided the light from the darkness. Later, in 3:20, why did Adam call his wife’s name Eve?
prompt.child: After God spoke to the man and the woman, Adam gave his wife a name. Why did he call her Eve?
prompt.teen: Genesis 3:20: “Adam called his wife’s name Eve, because she was” what?
prompt.older: Read with 1:4, why does 3:20 say Adam called his wife Eve?

choices.text: the lady of the garden walk
the giver of all the names

verses.text: And God saw the light, that it was good; and God divided the light from the darkness.
And Adam called his wife’s name Eve, because she was the mother of all living.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 20.
explanation.teen: 1:4 is the dividing of light; 3:20 gives the name and the reason. Read the reason.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:16 speaks of her bringing forth children. 1:4 says God saw the light, that it was good.
teaching.takeaway: Adam called her Eve because she was the mother of all living.

prompt.adult: In Genesis 3:12 the man says the woman gave him of the tree. Earlier, in 2:23, what does Adam say of her first, in the opening of his words?
prompt.child: When God first brought the woman to Adam, he spoke about her. What did he call her first?
prompt.older: Read with 3:12, what does 2:23 say she is, in the first phrase of his words?

verses.text: And Adam said: “This is now bone of my bones And flesh of my flesh; She shall be called Woman, Because she was taken out of Man.”
Then the man said, “The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.”

explanation.child: Look right after “This is now” in verse 23.
explanation.teen: 3:12 is the man’s later word; 2:23 gives two phrases about her. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:23 also says, “She shall be called Woman.” 3:12 says, “she gave me of the tree, and I ate.”
teaching.takeaway: Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones.”

prompt.adult: Genesis 1:17 says God set the lights in the firmament. In 2:1, when the heavens and the earth were finished, what else was finished with them?
prompt.child: After the days of making, the heavens and the earth were finished. What else does the verse say was finished with them?
prompt.teen: Genesis 2:1: “Thus the heavens and the earth, and” what, “were finished”?
prompt.older: Read with 1:17, what does 2:1 say was finished along with the heavens and the earth?

verses.text: God set them in the firmament of the heavens to give light on the earth,
Thus the heavens and the earth, and all the host of them, were finished.

explanation.child: Look at the words between “and the earth, and” and “were finished.”
explanation.teen: 1:17 is the placing of the lights; 2:1 names what was finished. Read the middle phrase.
explanation.older: It follows “and the earth, and” in 2:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:17 says the lights were to give light on the earth. 2:1 is the close of that work.
teaching.takeaway: The heavens and the earth, and all the host of them, were finished.

prompt.adult: Genesis 3:16 speaks to the woman of sorrow and conception. Earlier, in 1:27, after “So God created man,” how does the verse next describe that making?
prompt.child: The first chapter tells how God made man. After “So God created man,” how does the verse next describe that making?
prompt.teen: Genesis 1:27: after “So God created man,” what does it say next?
prompt.older: Read with 3:16, after “So God created man,” what does 1:27 say next?

verses.text: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
To the woman He said: “I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception; In pain you shall bring forth children; Your desire shall be for your husband, And he shall rule over you.”

explanation.child: Look at the words just after “So God created man” in verse 27.
explanation.teen: 3:16 is the word to the woman; 1:27 names how God created man. Read the words after “So God created man.”
explanation.older: It follows “So God created man” in 1:27.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:27 also says, “male and female He created them.” 3:16 says, “In pain you shall bring forth children.”
teaching.takeaway: God created him in the image of God.
